recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If PA wants a new graphical swimlane diagram in addition to the existing tables, that should be raised as a new editorial/design decision rather than treated as unreconciled FHIR-6105 work.
issue_request: FHIR-6105 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request for FHIR-core Appointment asking for the dense Appointment notes/status-transition section to use a chart, swimlane diagram, or other visual aid. The final resolution was to significantly update the status transition notes with tables and expand introductory text for the workflow and AppointmentResponse pattern; an additional diagram was only a possible QA enhancement.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in 2015 source history. Commit 85e9c099b91eab3ae119c8af3bd0f740581ef247, tagged Tracker# 6105 and 7669, converted the first Appointment status-transition prose into a grid table. Commit 42d02e5ebbf5e0b2d8bdd94463554afaa1502a32, tagged Tracker# 7669, 6105, and 7988, expanded the Appointment request/response introduction and converted additional Appointment status flows into tables.
additional_context: Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini and the current source/appointment fragments still contain the tabular status-flow examples and request/response pattern text. FHIR-7988 asked essentially the same diagram question for the same section and records that attempted diagrams were replaced by clearer tables. FHIR-7669 was a supporting clarification issue for Appointment requests, while FHIR-6938 and FHIR-5713 were background status-flow/status-code issues in the same 2015 PA reconciliation cluster. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting discussion, and Jira follow-up search found no relevant later reversal.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build source already implements the accepted table-based clarification and expanded introductory guidance, and adding a new diagram now would be optional editorial/design work rather than a necessary correction to current specification behavior.
